extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of Catholic catechism / parish or school religious instruction
extracted.subtask_description: A catechetical lesson describing how to identify the true (Roman Catholic) Church: its definition, four marks (one, holy, catholic, apostolic), three attributes (authority, infallibility, indefectibility), and related liturgical and doctrinal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church is the congregation of all those who profess the faith of Christ, partake of the same Sacraments, and are governed by their lawful pastors under one visible head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains 'congregation' (not the building), 'partake' (receive the Sacraments), 'lawful pastors' (each priest in his parish, each bishop in his diocese, the Pope universally), and 'visible head' (someone who can be seen — the Pope as vicar of Christ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks of the Church (one, holy, catholic, apostolic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church has four marks by which it may be known: it is one; it is holy; it is catholic; it is apostolic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any one of the marks is wanting, the church is not the true Church established by Christ. The text asserts the Roman Catholic Church alone can show all four marks. Use the four marks as the standard test when comparing religions/churches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of the Church (authority, infallibility, indefectibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The attributes of the Church are three: authority, infallibility, and indefectibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attributes 'flow from' the marks and are easier to deduce from the marks than to observe directly. They apply to the Church as founded by Christ and are treated individually in subsequent entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: By the authority of the Church is meant the right and power which the Pope and the bishops, as the successors of the Apostles, have to teach and govern the faithful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority is explained as the power to exact obedience; all authority ultimately comes from God. Resisting or disobeying lawful Church authority is equated with resisting God. Examples and analogies used: teacher over scholars, civil government officials after election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infallibility of the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: By the infallibility of the Church is meant that the Church cannot err when it teaches a doctrine of faith or morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that infallibility applies when the Pope teaches 'ex cathedra' as successor of St. Peter or when Pope and bishops united in general council teach on faith or morals. The Pope is not infallible outside teaching on faith and morals (e.g., in science, grammar). The Holy Ghost is promised to guide the Church so it will not err in such teachings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for papal infallibility (ex cathedra)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three things are required for the Pope to speak ex cathedra (infallibly): (1) he must speak as the head of the whole Church, not as a private person; (2) what he says must hold good for the whole Church (for all the faithful); (3) he must speak on matters of faith or morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides practical criteria for recognizing an ex cathedra statement (role, universal scope, and subject matter). Also warns that the Pope can err in non-faith-and-morals matters and can sin personally; infallibility pertains strictly to doctrinal teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefectibility of the Church
rubrics_metrics.description: By the indefectibility of the Church is meant that the Church, as Christ founded it, will last till the end of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Means the Church cannot change doctrines given by Our Lord nor ever cease to exist. Distinguishes between divine laws (unchangeable: e.g., number of Sacraments) and ecclesiastical laws (changeable: e.g., observance rules such as days when meat is not eaten).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible head of the Church (the Pope / Bishop of Rome)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Holy Father the Pope, the Bishop of Rome, is the vicar of Christ on earth and the visible head of the Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that the Bishop of Rome is always the Pope (successor of St. Peter); other bishops are successors of other Apostles. 'Vicar' means one who holds another's place and acts in his name. The Pope's authority mirrors St. Peter's primacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liturgical requirement: altar stone and relics for Mass
rubrics_metrics.description: In every altar the table, or flat part on which the priest celebrates Mass, should be of stone; if the altar is made of wood, then at least the part just in front of the tabernacle must be of stone and large enough to hold say two chalices (about ten or twelve inches square). In this stone are placed some relics of the holy martyrs; unless it is in the altar the priest cannot say Mass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes the ritual for placing relics: a piece is cut out of the stone, relic placed in the opening, the bishop replaces and seals the piece, blesses the stone, and gives it to the Church. The altar stone is normally covered by the altar cloth and must be present for Mass to be licit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation of Church membership and its relation to salvation
rubrics_metrics.description: All are bound to belong to the Church, and he who knows the Church to be the true Church and remains out of it, cannot be saved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains exceptions/nuances: a non-Catholic who was validly baptized and never committed mortal sin after Baptism might be saved because baptized persons are children of the Church; however, lacking confession, perfect contrition is required to remove mortal sin, which is difficult without Catholic instruction. If one doubts the truth of his church, he must settle the doubt and seek the true Church.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of the Church ('one')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church is one because all its members agree in one faith, are all in one communion, and are all under one head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is in government (hierarchy: pastor → bishop → archbishop → primate → Pope) and in doctrine (all Catholics believe the same truths). If any Catholic denies an article of faith he ceases to be Catholic. Contrasts with Protestant disunity and the right claimed by Protestants to interpret Scripture individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holiness of the Church ('holy')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church is holy because its founder, Jesus Christ, is holy; because it teaches a holy doctrine, invites all to a holy life, and because of the eminent holiness of so many thousands of its children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses examples and contrasts (criticism of certain Protestant doctrines as insufficiently holy). Holiness is judged by doctrine, invitation to holy life, and the existence of canonized saints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catholicity/universality of the Church ('catholic')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church is catholic or universal because it subsists in all ages, teaches all nations, and maintains all truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains universality in time (continuous existence), place (not confined to one region), and doctrine (same doctrines and sacraments everywhere). Notes practical reasons for Latin usage (uniformity across nations and ages) and the advantage of a single liturgical language for councils and universal governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apostolicity of the Church ('apostolic')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Church is apostolic because it was founded by Christ on His Apostles and is governed by their lawful successors, and because it has never ceased, and never will cease, to teach their doctrine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes unbroken succession from the Apostles to current bishops and Popes (example: enumeration of Popes back to St. Peter). Apostolic succession underpins the Church's authority to make laws, ordain priests, and administer sacraments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal temporal power for independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope should have some city or states, not belonging to any government, in which he would be the chief and only ruler (temporal power), so that he may be free and independent in governing the Church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues historical basis (Papal States) and practical need (independence from secular rulers to speak and act freely). Uses analogy to the U.S. federal district (District of Columbia). Notes practical uses of temporal possessions: support missions, educate priests, print books, and fund Church works; mentions 'Peter's pence' as current substitute for former Papal possessions.
